new_leaves.label: Flatstyle
new_leaves.defn: Twentieth-century Native American easel painting in opaque watercolour with flat, outlined colour and little shading or perspective, showing dances, ceremonies and daily life: the San Ildefonso watercolourists (1910s), Hopi painters, the Kiowa Six (Southern Plains style), Dorothy Dunn's Studio at the Santa Fe Indian School (1932–62) and the Bacone school.

new_leaves.defn: Buddhist hanging scrolls painted in mineral colours and gold on silk in Goryeo Korea, chiefly 13th–14th century, often coloured from both sides of the silk, most now in Japanese temples: Water-Moon Avalokiteshvara, Amitabha triads, Ksitigarbha, arhats.

new_leaves.defn: Japanese woodblock-printed picture books of the Edo and Meiji periods, from illustrated tales to colour-printed kyōka anthologies, painting manuals and sketchbooks: Moronobu's picture books, Utamaro's Picture Book of Selected Insects (1788), the Hokusai Manga.
